title: POC scoping - benchmark harness integration - Atlas FinTech
summary: POC scoping call to align on benchmark goals, workload sizing, harness integration approach, streaming vs non-streaming tests, success criteria, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Customer will provide sample request scripts and dataset slices; Redwood to provide benchmark template, k6/locust adapters, and a GA-compatible harness repo. Security and VPC/KMS questions noted.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-09-21 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Aaron Diaz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Atlas - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Atlas - Platform), Nora Ruiz (Atlas - SecOps), Jason Kim (Atlas - Infra)

Auto-generated summary: align on benchmarks and harness integration, action items to share templates and schedule pilot kickoff.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya at Redwood, and uh Aaron and Jordan are with me on the engineering side. before we jump in can we do quick round robin, Sarah?
[00:18] Sarah Patel: Yeah hi, Sarah here, head of ML at Atlas, we own the user-facing assistant and want to validate latency/cost tradeoffs for a production rollout, thanks for hosting.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, platform, i'll own the load tests and infra side of the POC.
[00:40] Nora Ruiz: Nora, secops, i'll be looking at encryption, audit logs, and VPC details.
[00:48] Maya Chen: Great, goal for today is to align on success criteria, workload sizing, and how your existing scripts plug into our benchmark harness. we'll also cover streaming vs non streaming results and timeline.
[01:05] Aaron Diaz: Quick note, we usually run both streaming and non-streaming passes because they exercise different codepaths and the latency metrics are different — streaming shows per-token latency and tail for first token, non-streaming shows end-to-end completion latency.
[01:25] Sarah Patel: Perfect, we're particularly sensitive to p95 and p99 for interactive flows, p50 is nice but not sufficient. target is p95 < 350ms for short chats (<= 128 tokens) and p99 < 700ms ideally, while keeping unit cost below our current provider.
[01:50] Aaron Diaz: Ok noted. can you share current RPS and concurrency?
[01:58] Jason Kim: currently prod peek is about 200 rps for the assistant, with concurrency around 1.2k active websockets during peak. for the POC we want to test steady 200 rps and bursts up to 600 rps to validate autoscaling.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: that's helpful. for the harness we recommend two workload profiles: steady-state (200 rps) for 15 minutes and burst tests (ramp to 600 rps over 60s, hold 3m). we'll also do long-run prefix-cache tests for conversation-heavy workloads to check KV cache hit behavior.
[02:40] Sarah Patel: on scripts we have Locust and some internal python loadgen that uses asyncio; can Redwood run those or prefer k6?
[02:52] Aaron Diaz: We support k6 and Locust out of the box; for custom python scripts we can wrap them in a container and include them in the harness. easiest is you drop your request generator and a small sample dataset in the shared repo.
[03:08] Liam O'Connor: what's the expected format? we have JSON lines with prompt templates and user metadata.
[03:16] Maya Chen: JSONL is perfect. we'll give you a benchmark template that shows required fields: prompt, max_tokens, stop, temperature, and a customer_id field for grouping. we'll also provide an adapter script for your python loadgen.
[03:32] Nora Ruiz: Sec question: how do you handle data at rest and keys for private deployments? we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for the POC.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: For Private we support customer-managed KMS and you can run a private control plane; audit logs are available and we'll export them to your S3/GCS. For hosted/de dedicated we have envelope encryption and rotation, but for this pilot we can scope a VPC peering option.
[04:00] Sarah Patel: good. also curious about model variants — we'll want cost parity comparisons between optimized 8-bit quantized variants and full fp16.
[04:12] Aaron Diaz: We'll run paired benchmarks: same prompts across model variants and report tokens/sec, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll include quantized runs and one run with KV cache primed to show savings for multi-turn flows.
[04:32] Jason Kim: for metric collection what do you emit? we need per-request id, start/finish timestamps, model name/version, batch size, and whether streaming was used.
[04:44] Maya Chen: yes we'll emit request_id, timestamps, model, seq_len, batch_size, gpu_type, and token counts. streaming runs will also log per-chunk latency.
[04:56] Sarah Patel: timeline wise, we want POC kickoff within 2 weeks and wrap the 4-week pilot with a decision meeting after that. is that workable?
[05:05] Maya Chen: Yes. proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) align and exchange scripts + access, week 1 Redwood runs initial small-scale bench to validate harness, week 2 full-scale runs and iterations, weeks 3-4 optimization and final report.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: we'll need a playbook for how to execute the harness in our VPC for the private scenario.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: we'll share a VPC deployment guide — step-by-step scripts to spin up the runner, IAM roles, and KMS config. it typically takes 1-2 days to deploy and smoke test.
[05:42] Nora Ruiz: also require SOC2 attestation and an export of PenTest summary before we start, can you share those docs?
[05:50] Maya Chen: yes i'll attach our security pack, SOC 2 report, and the pen test executive summary.
[05:58] Sarah Patel: for success criteria let's make it explicit: 1) p95 chat latency <= 350ms on non-streaming for short prompts, 2) streaming first-token latency <= 120ms, 3) cost per 1k tokens <= X (we'll share current numbers privately), 4) KV cache hit reduces token processing by at least 30% on multi-turn bench.
[06:25] Aaron Diaz: we'll instrument all of those and produce a benchmark dashboard. note that streaming numbers depend heavily on network and chunking strategy — we'll include fixed-chunk and adaptive-chunk runs.
[06:40] Jason Kim: question about autoscaling — in Dedicated mode, how predictable is throughput when you have shared pools?
[06:48] Jordan Lee: dedicated pools are isolated; you get reserved throughput. for hosted we have routing policies and fallbacks which may route to cheaper variants during capacity constraints. for POC we'll recommend dedicated reserved nodes so results are stable and repeatable.
[07:05] Sarah Patel: can you run GPU-level microbenchmarks too? like per-GPU throughput by sequence length?
[07:12] Aaron Diaz: yes we'll include microbenchmarks by seq len (32/64/128/512) and show tokens/sec and memory footprint.
[07:22] Liam O'Connor: on our side i'll provision a test VPC, share example JSONL with 10k prompts sampled from prod, and we can provide a locustfile and our internal asyncio runner.
[07:34] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll send the benchmark template + harness README and a k6/locust example.
[07:40] Sarah Patel: any known gotchas?
[07:44] Aaron Diaz: sometimes prompt normalization leads to slight perf diffs, and KV cache warmup needs careful priming — we'll provide recommended priming sequences. also watch for tokenization differences across model variants.
[07:58] Nora Ruiz: last sec question — will logs include PII? we need to ensure sampling or masking before logs leave our environment.
[08:07] Jordan Lee: we can support client-side masking or run the harness in your VPC so logs never leave your network. we'll document masking options.
[08:18] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and action items.
[08:22] Aaron Diaz: quick note on benchmark passes: we'll do baseline (non-streaming), streaming (per-token traces), quantized run, and KV-cache primed run. expected total run time for full suite ~3-4 hours but we'll split across multiple short windows to avoid skew from infra churn.
[08:42] Sarah Patel: great. thanks everyone.

End transcript.
